text: Unpacking pulls values out of a sequence and into variables, in one line.
First takes the head, last takes the tail, and star middle absorbs everything between.
Star middle always becomes a list, even when it catches nothing at all.
You can only use one star in a target list, since two would be ambiguous.
So first and last are one and five.
And middle is two, three, four, collected automatically.
Unpacking also gives you the cleanest swap in any language.
a, b equals b, a. The right side is built first, so no temporary variable is needed.
Two and one, swapped without a third name.
Double star unpacks dictionaries, and later keys win over earlier ones.
That makes it the neatest way to override defaults without mutating the original.
So colour becomes blue while size keeps its default of M.
Up next, sets. Comment PYTHON if you want the cheat sheet.
